# FretShed

> FretShed is a guitar practice app for iPhone, iPad and Mac. Pick a genre, key and tempo, and it generates a fresh guitar solo over a backing track. You then work the solo out by ear, with no tabs or notation. It's built for guitarists who are serious about progress and want to get past playing the same licks.

FretShed is made by Decibel Technologies Limited, a company registered in England and Wales. It's on the App Store for iPhone and iPad, and on the Mac App Store.

## What it does

- Generates a new guitar solo on demand in rock, blues, jazz, metal or funk, in any major or minor key, from 60 to 120 bpm. Each solo plays over a backing track and is never repeated.
- Gives you no tabs and no notation on purpose. You learn each solo by listening, which trains your ear.
- Loops a phrase from point A to point B, and slows playback to as low as 50% speed without changing the pitch.
- Includes an Ear Tuner that you tune by listening rather than by watching a needle. Tunings are standard, E♭ standard, drop D, drop D♭ and DADGAD.
- Includes a metronome with adjustable tempo and time signature.
- Includes a recorder that keeps running when you switch tabs or lock the screen, and that you can stop from the Lock Screen.
- Syncs your saved solos, recordings, stars and loop points across iPhone, iPad and Mac, audio included, for subscribers.

## Pricing

- Free to try.
- FretShed Pro Monthly: $14.99 a month.
- FretShed Pro Yearly: $149.99 a year, about $12.50 a month.
- Pro includes 80 fresh solos every 30 days on a rolling window, all five genres, and every feature on iPhone, iPad and Mac with one subscription.

## Who it's for

- Guitarists who want to improve their ear and their improvising, not collect tabs.
- Players who need a solo to work from quickly, for example for a gig or a jam.
- Players stuck on the same licks who want unfamiliar material to learn by ear.
